categories.label: Safety failures
categories.blurb: The system violates some aspect of the specification.

items.label: Incorrect synchronization
items.description: Required synchronization is missing, misplaced, or incorrectly scoped. Includes race conditions, incorrect atomicity assumptions, unsafe publication, and incorrect memory-ordering assumptions.

items.label: Incorrect task partitioning or scheduling
items.description: Work is skipped, duplicated, assigned to overlapping output regions, or executed in an order that violates dependencies.

items.label: Incorrect reductions
items.summary: Partial results combined the wrong way.
items.description: Partial results are lost, counted multiple times, combined incorrectly, or combined in an order that violates required numerical accuracy or reproducibility.

items.label: Incorrect dependency assumptions
items.description: Tasks or loop iterations assumed to be independent actually depend on the results or side effects of other tasks.

items.label: Unsafe object or resource lifetime
items.summary: Access after free, move, or close.
items.description: A worker accesses an object after it has been freed, moved, resized, closed, or otherwise invalidated by another worker.

items.label: Use of thread-unsafe components
items.summary: A component used outside its safe pattern.
items.description: A library, API, data structure, or runtime service is used concurrently even though it does not support the relevant access pattern.

items.label: Incorrect error or cancellation handling
items.summary: Failures lost, cancellation leaves a mess.
items.description: Worker failures are lost or ignored, partial updates violate invariants, or cancellation leaves work and resources in an inconsistent state.

items.label: Unintended nondeterminism
items.summary: Relies on an order that isn't guaranteed.
items.description: The program incorrectly relies on a particular execution order, result order, or timing relationship that the parallel runtime does not guarantee.

categories.label: Performance failures
categories.blurb: The system fails to deliver the expected latency, throughput, efficiency, speedup, or scalability.

items.label: Excessive synchronization
items.description: Locks, atomics, barriers, memory fences, or other coordination operations are used more frequently, or with stronger guarantees, than necessary — serializing execution and increasing coherence overhead.

items.label: Poor task partitioning or scheduling
items.description: Work is divided too unevenly, tasks are too fine-grained, or the scheduling policy poorly matches the workload, causing load imbalance, idle workers, or excessive scheduling overhead.

items.label: Oversubscription
items.summary: More workers than the hardware can host.
items.description: The program creates more runnable workers than the available hardware can efficiently support, causing context switching, cache disruption, and scheduler overhead.

items.label: Memory bottlenecks
items.description: The program suffers from poor locality, memory-bandwidth saturation, excessive cache-coherence traffic, or NUMA-unaware data placement, so adding threads provides little or no speedup.

items.label: Shared-resource contention
items.summary: Workers queue for a bounded resource.
items.description: Workers compete for allocators, I/O devices, network bandwidth, database connections, GPU queues, or other bounded resources.

items.label: Insufficient useful parallelism
items.summary: Not enough independent work to scale.
items.description: Serial bottlenecks, limited available concurrency, or an unsuitable parallel algorithm prevent the program from scaling (includes Amdahl's law limitations).

categories.label: Liveness failures
categories.blurb: A required event or state is never eventually reached.

items.label: Deadlock
items.summary: Workers wait on each other forever.
items.description: Workers wait indefinitely for locks, resources, messages, or events that cannot occur because of a circular or otherwise unsatisfiable dependency.

items.label: Livelock
items.description: Workers continue executing and reacting to one another but repeatedly retry, back off, or discard work without making useful progress.

items.label: Starvation
items.summary: One worker never gets its turn.
items.description: A worker or task is indefinitely denied CPU time, access to a lock, access to a resource, or an opportunity to perform required work.

items.label: Incorrect termination detection
items.summary: Stops too early, or waits too long.
items.description: The program either waits after all work has finished or declares completion while outstanding work can still generate additional work.

items.label: Broken progress assumptions
items.summary: Assumes fairness the runtime won't give.
items.description: The algorithm assumes fairness, prompt scheduling, eventual lock acquisition, or guaranteed progress that the runtime or synchronization mechanism does not provide.
